mcp-abap-adt/search.semantic: Start, wait for, or end a debug session of an ABAP program or AMDP method.

description: [read-only] Debugger listener and session. Each operation up to end sends one SAP request, the operation's, and answers what SAP answered. kind abap: checkListener answers whether another debugger holds this identity's debugging (SAP's 409 names the holder); listen waits for a debuggee for exactly hold_seconds, SAP's hold, and answers the debuggee caught (debuggee_id, its server) or caught: false; a breakpoint stops a program while a listen is open; stopListener ends the listener and deletes the identity's breakpoints; attach attaches debuggee_id on the attaching session, which the first attach opens and every later attach, step and reading uses; detachDebugger sends detachDebugger on the attaching session, which releases the debuggee, and the program runs on; terminateDebuggee ends the debuggee where it stands and terminateDebugger frees the debugger; each answers SAP's answer as it came, which is a 500 when it succeeded, and the next answer shows the success (noSessionAttached, or the program's end); setDebuggerSettings sends the settings given at the attached debuggee. kind amdp: start opens an AMDP session for the connected SAP user and answers its main_id; getEvents answers the events SAP sends (breaks with their debuggee ids, breakpoint confirmations, ends); stop ends the AMDP session; deleteDebuggee cancels the execution of debuggee_id. end, for either kind, takes state_handle and logs off each connection the debug state opened, one logoff each: an attached debuggee runs on, an AMDP debug session ends, and the user's breakpoints stay set until stopListener removes them; the debug state and its handle end with it, and a new debug state of either kind and any identity opens after it. The answer carries state_handle while the debug state holds something, and for abap the identity in force. Runs outside batch mode.

debuggee_id.description: abap attach: the debuggee_id listen answered. amdp deleteDebuggee: the debuggee id of a break event.

debugging_mode.description: abap: user (when omitted) catches every request of the request user; terminal catches the requests that carry this debug state's terminal_id and ide_id. The first abap call of a debug state fixes it.

detail.description: How much of the answer to return: "terse" (default, the fields you need to act), "full" (the whole parse), "raw" (the document as ADT sent it).

hold_seconds.description: abap listen: how long SAP holds the listen, in seconds; SAP answers at a catch or when the hold ends.

kind.description: abap works with the ABAP debugger; amdp with the AMDP debugger of SQLScript methods.

operation.description: The one request: abap checkListener, listen, stopListener, attach, detachDebugger, terminateDebuggee, terminateDebugger or setDebuggerSettings; amdp start, getEvents, stop or deleteDebuggee. end, for either kind, logs off the debug state.

request_user.description: abap, user mode: the SAP user whose requests the breakpoints and the listener catch; the connected SAP user when omitted. The first abap call of a debug state fixes it.

server.description: abap attach: the debuggee's application server, as listen answered it.

settings.description: abap setDebuggerSettings: the settings sent; a field left out keeps its value.

create_exception_object.description: Creates the exception object even where a CATCH does not ask for it.

system_debugging.description: Steps into system programs and stops at breakpoints there.

state_handle.description: The handle of this server's debug state. abap checkListener, listen, stopListener and attach, and amdp start, open the debug state when it is omitted and answer its handle; every other operation takes it.

take_over.description: abap listen: true displaces another debugger listening for the same user; false, or omitted, answers its 409. amdp start: true ends an AMDP session of this user left behind.

name: HandlerDebugSession
